les: Iemand om na op te kyk
kaps_punt: Weeklikse lees deur leerders: lees vir genot: Lees oor rolmodelle of suksesvolle mense/mense met selfvertroue.

items.bewering: Siya Kolisi het as klein seun op 'n growwe veld in Zwide rugby gespeel.
items.bron: The42 / AFP, Nov 2019 (https://www.the42.ie/siya-kolisi-south-africa-rugby-world-cup-4885947-Nov2019/): he first handled a ball in Zwide on 'a gravel, often wind-swept school sport field'; coach Eric Songwiqi calls it 'a rough, hard, gravel pitch'; uncle Vukile Kolisi: 'rough, dusty pitches'.

items.bewering: Zwide is 'n township in die stad wat ons vandag Gqeberha noem.
items.bron: Wikipedia (Siya Kolisi): 'Zwide, iBhayi, a township in Port Elizabeth'; SAnews.gov.za, 'Name change shakeup for the Eastern Cape' (Feb 2021): Port Elizabeth officially renamed Gqeberha, gazetted 23 Feb 2021.

items.bewering: Hy is in 1991 daar gebore
items.bron: SA History Online (https://www.sahistory.org.za/people/siyamthanda-kolisi): born 16 June 1991 'in Zwide Township in Port Elizabeth'. Wikipedia gives birthplace as Port Elizabeth, of which Zwide is part.

items.bewering: en het by sy ouma grootgeword.
items.bron: SAHO: 'raised by his paternal grandmother'; Wikipedia: grandmother Nolulamile raised him; The Citizen long read (citizen.co.za, 'The incredible journey of Siya Kolisi'): lived with grandmother, aunt and uncle in Zwide.

items.bewering: Daar was dikwels min kos in die huis en geen geld vir rugbyskoene nie.
items.bron: The Citizen long read: 'Going hungry was hardly a weird feeling'; grandmother cleaned kitchens 'to scrape together enough money for the odd meal'. The42 / AFP: uncle says he 'did not have rugby boots'. France24 (2 Nov 2019) quoting Bryan Habana: worried less about boots than 'what food he was going to eat that night'.

items.bewering: Party aande was daar niks om te eet nie, en hy het honger gaan slaap.
items.bron: Big Issue South Africa, 'The Kolisis' mission to change lives' (bigissue.org.za): frequent nights without a meal; Kolisi: 'going to bed without food in your stomach is one thing I don't wish upon anybody'. Dispatch Live / Herald, 29 Apr 2020: 'There is nothing worse than hunger'.

items.bewering: Siya het by African Bombers, 'n klub in sy eie buurt, leer rugby speel.
items.bron: SAHO: at seven he 'joined the local rugby team, African Bombers Rugby Club'; SA Rugby Magazine (sarugbymag.co.za/?p=132592): the club was 'based at Dan Qeqe Stadium only a few streets from his house'.

items.bewering: Hy het sy eerste wedstryde vir die klub kaalvoet gespeel.
items.bron: The42 / AFP, Nov 2019: uncle Vukile Kolisi says Siya 'grew up playing rugby barefooted on rough, dusty pitches' and at nine came home with bleeding feet because he 'did not have rugby boots'. He joined Bombers at seven (SAHO), so his early club matches fall in that barefoot period. No source ties the barefoot detail to the club by name; the claim rests on the family account, which is consistent with it.

items.bewering: Hy is later vir die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan gekies. Daardie span het by 'n groot toernooi in Mosselbaai gaan speel.
items.bron: The Citizen long read: 'picked for Eastern Province's Under-12 B side for a provincial tournament in Mossel Bay'; The Citizen, 'Kolisi's U12 coach says...' (Eric Songwiqi): 'Siya made the EP U12 team. He went to the interprovincial tournament in Mossel Bay'. Wikipedia: impressed scouts at a youth tournament in Mossel Bay at 12. (It was the B side; 'die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan' is a fair simplification.)

items.bewering: Grey Junior, 'n skool uit die stad, het ook daar gespeel. Die skool se afrigters het hom daardie dag sien speel.
items.bron: No source places a Grey Junior school team at the Mossel Bay tournament, and the sources disagree on where and by whom Grey noticed him. Songwiqi calls Mossel Bay an INTERPROVINCIAL tournament (provincial sides, not schools). The Citizen long read puts his match against Grey Junior separately, as a game for Emsengeni Primary that Grey won by about 50-0, and says the bursary came from Andrew Hayidakis. A Good Things Guy account ('Growing Up Grey', reached only through search excerpts) says Grey first noticed him when his club played a Grey Junior side in a local tournament months BEFORE Mossel Bay. Wikipedia says only that he 'impressed scouts' at Mossel Bay. The scene the lesson builds (Grey Junior playing at Mossel Bay, its coaches watching him there that day) is supported by none of these. A wording that every source fits: he played well at the Mossel Bay tournament, and afterwards Grey Junior offered him a bursary. Searched in English and Afrikaans.

items.bewering: Hulle het vir hom 'n beurs aangebied om by Grey Junior te kom leer.
items.bron: Wikipedia: 'offered a scholarship at Grey Junior in Port Elizabeth' at 12; SAHO: 'received a scholarship at ... Grey Junior School in PE'; SA Rugby Magazine: 'offered a scholarship at Grey Junior when he was 12'. (The Citizen long read names Grey High; he went to Grey Junior in Grade 7 and then on to Grey High.) Only the 'Hulle' (the coaches who watched him) depends on the onseker item above.

items.bewering: Siya moes sy ouma se huis verlaat
items.bron: Most sources say his grandmother Nolulamile died in his arms when he was about 12 (the Jonathan Ball biography 'Against All Odds', via search excerpts; the Irish Mail on Sunday, 2018, says eight), and that an aunt then raised him (Kolisi, in an autobiography extract, SA Rugby Magazine: 'After my grandmother died my aunt raised me'). He went to Grey Junior at 12, in Grade 7. No source settles whether she was still alive when he left. Read with 'het by sy ouma grootgeword' and nothing about her death, the sentence tells a learner that he left his living grandmother, which may be false. 'The house in Zwide' would hold either way.

items.bewering: en in 'n koshuis gaan bly.
items.bron: The Citizen long read: 'a boy in his hostel, Nick Holton, took him under his wings'.

items.bewering: In sy nuwe klas het almal Engels gepraat, en hy het min daarvan verstaan. Hy moes die taal van die begin af leer
items.bron: SAHO: at Grey Junior he 'could not speak a word of English'; classmate Nicholas Holton taught him English and Kolisi taught him isiXhosa. The Citizen long read: 'initially couldn't speak a word of English'.

items.bewering: Sy ma is oorlede terwyl hy nog op skool was.
items.bron: France24 (2 Nov 2019): his mother 'died when he was 15'; The Citizen long read: Phakama died when he was 15; SAHO says 16. Either age falls while he was at Grey High (he played U18 Craven Week in 2009 and joined the WP academy at 18 in 2010; Wikipedia). Wikipedia's siblings section gives 2009, which would still be his school years.

items.bewering: Ná skool het hy vir 'n groot span in Kaapstad begin speel.
items.bron: SAHO: joined the Western Province Rugby Institute in 2010 and won the U19 Currie Cup with WP that year; Wikipedia: senior WP debut 2011, Stormers squad 2012. Both are Cape Town teams. (The academy itself was in Stellenbosch, which the lesson does not claim otherwise.)

items.bewering: In 2013 het hy sy eerste toetswedstryd vir die Springbokke gespeel.
items.bron: Wikipedia: Test debut 15 June 2013 against Scotland at Mbombela Stadium, Nelspruit; SAHO: 2013 debut against Scotland in Nelspruit.

items.bewering: Toe hy drie-en-twintig was, het hy sy jonger suster en broer by hom ingeneem.
items.bron: Wikipedia: half-siblings Liyema and Liphelo have lived in the Kolisi household since 2014. Irish Mail on Sunday, 3 June 2018 (via search excerpt): 'aged 23, became their legal guardian'. City Press, 2016: custody 'two years ago'. Born June 1991, so 2014 is consistent with 23. They are half-siblings (same mother); 'jonger suster en broer' is accurate.

items.bewering: In 2018 het die afrigter hom as kaptein van die Springbokke aangewys.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 28 May 2018, 'Kolisi to be first black South Africa Test captain': coach Rassie Erasmus announced it; Wikipedia: named captain 28 May 2018.

items.bewering: Hy was die eerste swart speler wat die span in 'n toetswedstryd gelei het.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 28 May 2018: 'will become the first black Test captain of South Africa'; Wikipedia: first black captain in the team's 126-year history, first led in a Test against England, 9 June 2018; SAHO: 'the first black player to captain the Springboks'. One report (via search) says he had already led the side briefly in a 2017 Test when Eben Etzebeth was injured. That makes him the first black player to lead in a Test either way, so the superlative holds.

items.bewering: Aan die einde van Mei 2019 het hy sy knie by Newlands lelik beseer.
items.bron: The Herald (theherald.co.za, 25 May 2019, 'Jantjies stars as Stormers down Highlanders'): played at DHL Newlands on 25 May 2019 and Kolisi 'hobbled off shortly before halftime'. TimesLIVE, 30 May 2019: injured his knee scoring a try against the Highlanders, out for the rest of Super Rugby, in a brace for six weeks instead of surgery.

items.bewering: Hy kon daarna omtrent drie maande lank nie speel nie.
items.bron: Business Day, 12 Aug 2019, 'Captain Kolisi back for the Boks': he returned for Western Province against the Pumas in the Currie Cup the weekend before (about 10 Aug), then played the Springbok Test against Argentina at Loftus on 17 Aug 2019. That is about 11-12 weeks after 25 May, so 'omtrent drie maande' holds.

items.bewering: Die Wêreldbeker in Japan sou net 'n paar maande later begin. ... Hy het betyds herstel en die span Japan toe gelei.
items.bron: rugby.com.au, 20 Sep 2019: the tournament opened with Japan v Russia on 20 September 2019 in Tokyo, under four months after the injury. Wikipedia: Kolisi captained South Africa at the 2019 World Cup.

items.bewering: Die Springbokke het die eerste wedstryd teen Nieu-Seeland met 13 punte teen 23 verloor.
items.bron: rugby.com.au, 21 Sep 2019, 'All Blacks hold out Springboks in brutal World Cup clash'; Sport24, 21 Sep 2019: New Zealand won 23-13 in Yokohama in the Pool B opener, South Africa's first match of the tournament.

items.bewering: Daarna het Suid-Afrika elke wedstryd gewen en tot in die eindstryd deurgedring.
items.bron: ESPN South Africa results 2019 (africa.espn.com) and World Rugby: Namibia 57-3, Italy 49-3, Canada 66-7, quarter-final Japan 26-3, semi-final Wales 19-16, then the final. No defeat after the opener.

items.bewering: Daar het hulle Engeland met 32 punte teen 12 geklop. Siya het as kaptein die goue beker bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: Wikipedia (Siya Kolisi; 2019 Rugby World Cup final): captained South Africa to a 32-12 win over England in Yokohama; SAnews.gov.za, 'SA crowned 2019 Rugby World Cup Champions'. World Rugby / rugby365: the Webb Ellis Cup is sterling silver with 24-carat gold plating, so 'goue beker' is a fair description of how it looks.

items.bewering: Die span het daarna met die beker deur die hele land getoer.
items.bron: SAnews.gov.za, 'Taste of victory' (Nov 2019) and News24 live coverage, 7-11 Nov 2019: the tour went to Pretoria, Johannesburg and Soweto, Durban, East London, Port Elizabeth and Cape Town, in four of the nine provinces. Daily Maverick, 10 Nov 2019, and Business Day: crowds in Port Elizabeth forced several stops to be cancelled, with a promised March 2020 return that never happened. 'Deur die hele land' overstates it, and a learner in a province the tour never reached will read it as false.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier. The team toured several big cities in the country with the cup (Pretoria, Johannesburg and Soweto, Durban, East London, Gqeberha and Cape Town), not the whole country. Something like 'het met die beker deur die land getoer' or 'het met die beker na groot stede in die land gegaan' is true.

items.bewering: 'n Oop bus met die beker het stadig deur Zwide se strate gery. Siya het die beker terug na die buurt van sy kinderdae gebring.
items.bron: Business Day, 10 Nov 2019, 'Siya Kolisi brings trophy to the township where it all began'; Daily Maverick, 10 Nov 2019, 'Huge turnout for Kolisi as Boks bring Webb Ellis Cup home to PE': the bus could hardly move in Koyana Street as thousands of Zwide residents lined the route. The42 / AFP: Kolisi held the trophy 'as an open-top bus crawled through the streets'.

items.bewering: Hy en sy vrou het kort daarna 'n stigting begin wat gesinne met kos help.
items.bron: Kolisi Foundation (kolisifoundation.org, 'What's in store for 2021?'): Siya and Rachel launched it in April 2020, about five months after the November 2019 tour, beginning with food parcels and vouchers; #Each1Feed1 gave families monthly food parcels; more than 32 800 parcels in 2020. Wikipedia: launched 2020, food insecurity among its focus areas. For the person signing off: the couple announced their separation in October 2024 (Cape Argus, 23 Oct 2024). The sentence describes 2020, when she was his wife, so it is true as written.

items.bewering: In 2023 het die Springbokke weer om die Wêreldbeker gespeel. Die eindstryd was in Frankryk, en hulle het met net een punt gewen.
items.bron: Wikipedia (2023 Rugby World Cup final); World Rugby, 'Rugby World Cup 2023 finals review': South Africa beat New Zealand 12-11 at the Stade de France (Saint-Denis, Paris) on 28 October 2023.

items.bewering: Siya het die goue beker daar vir die tweede keer bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: World Rugby, 2023 finals review: Kolisi lifted the Webb Ellis Cup for the second time as captain; Wikipedia: first South African captain to lift it twice.

items.bewering: beurs: Geld wat iemand anders vir jou skool of studie betaal.
items.bron: Regenesys, 'What is a bursary' (regenesys.net), and Old Mutual, 'Bursaries and scholarships' (oldmutual.co.za): a money award to pay for a student's schooling or study, usually not repaid. In this lesson Grey's full bursary 'covered every cost' (Good Things Guy, via search excerpt).

items.bewering: toetswedstryd: 'n Groot wedstryd tussen die nasionale spanne van twee lande.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Test match (rugby union)': an international match, usually between two senior national teams; Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'test match': a rugby or cricket match between the teams of two different countries. (Exceptions such as the British and Irish Lions are not relevant at Grade 4.)

items.bewering: eindstryd: Die laaste wedstryd van 'n toernooi, waarin die twee beste spanne teen mekaar speel.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Final (competition)': the match that decides the winner of the whole event, usually played between the winners of the two semi-finals; Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'final': 'the last of a series of games or competitions, in which the winner is decided'. A final is defined by who won through, not by who is best. The lesson's own story shows the gap: New Zealand beat South Africa in 2019 but did not reach the final, so a learner reading the entry with the story learns that the team that beat the Springboks was not one of the 'two best'.
items.regstelling: Define it by what it decides, not by 'beste': the last match of a tournament, played between the two teams that won all the rounds before it, and whoever wins it wins the tournament. Drop 'die twee beste spanne'.

items.bewering: stigting: 'n Groep wat geld insamel om ander mense te help.
items.bron: Wiktionary, 'stichting' (the Dutch cognate): a non-profit, (charitable) foundation; Wikipedia, 'Stichting': a non-profit body serving a public or social purpose. In this lesson's case the Kolisi Foundation takes general donations and runs fundraisers (kolisifoundation.org). It is a simplification, since some foundations spend their own capital rather than collecting money, but it is true for the foundation the lesson describes. No Afrikaans dictionary entry could be reached online.

opsomming: Almost all the biography checks out, including the first-black-Test-captain claim, but two details of how Grey Junior found him cannot be established: no source puts a Grey Junior team or its coaches at the Mossel Bay tournament, and 'he had to leave his grandmother's house' may imply a living grandmother when most sources say she died about when he went to Grey Junior. Two claims are false and need narrowing: the trophy tour did not go 'through the whole country', and the glossary says a final is between 'the two best teams'.
